body: Running Guardrails for the dogfooding should only be with our released version of Guardrails.  Never running it in the debugger.

Failures should be in the design to fail before the harness is run, if possible. (i.e. /guardrails-review should ensure that for the given plan, we have the potentially needed models, even with JIT judge model resolution).

Added to the Self-hosting hazard warn block, where you anchored it: dogfood with the RELEASED guardrails only, never a debug build or under the debugger. Reasoning recorded in the plan rather than just the rule — this stage edits the harness itself, so a locally-built guardrails verifies the plan with the very code the plan changes, and a pass or fail could come from an uncommitted edit either way. Also noted the released binary is the only configuration a user will ever have, which is what the dogfood is meant to measure.

Agreed, and I did not just soften item 2. Two changes: item 2 now says registry construction is the BACKSTOP not the gate (failing there means a wave is already in flight and work may be committed), and a new 'Failing early' section states the principle plus your /guardrails-review requirement explicitly, including the JIT judge case and why it is the hard one — a judge model resolved at judging time is by construction resolved after the work it judges was paid for. I did NOT decide where it lands: that expands scope into a skill change, so there is a new :::question ('fail-early-scope') with three options and my recommendation of the split — land the hook and static-model check now, defer JIT resolution to #223 where a judge can actually resolve to a non-Claude model. Please answer it in the page.
